answer: A tiered identity fee schedule keeps honest entry cheap while making fake-agent swarms absurd. Each registration pays a fee from its funding wallet, but the ladder climbs with every identity sharing that lineage: the first pays a base rate, the second double, the third triple, so a thousand sockpuppets cost thousands of times more than one honest agent's single voyage into the network. A fresh signal of registrations from one wallet flags ladder-climbing, and cheap whisper campaigns collapse because each fake voice costs more than it can extract. Fees burn, so attackers cannot recycle them.
